text:
Sam: FYI the Netlify preview for my docs PR is rendering but fonts are blocked by CORS on the preview URL: https://deploy-preview-123--docs.redwood.ai.netlify.app
Maria: saw that too, opened the preview. NetlifyBot says deploy succeeded but browser console shows "Access to font at '.../Inter.woff2' has been blocked by CORS"
Jake: probably missing _headers file in the site root or Netlify isn't sending Access-Control-Allow-Origin for /assets/fonts
Priya: yep we had a similar thing last quarter — we used a limited header for just fonts rather than wildcard for everything
Sam: can someone confirm the minimal fix? I can open a tiny PR to add headers + build script tweak
Maria: add a file at `site/_headers` with something like:
```
/assets/fonts/*
  Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
```
But please avoid `/*` if you care about cookies on other paths
Jake: also Netlify follows the `_headers` at publish time — if the CI step is doing `mkdocs build` into `site/`, ensure it copies `_headers` into the publish directory
Priya: our issue last time was `static/fonts` being a symlink in the repo. Netlify resolves symlinks differently. Quick fix is to copy the real files during the build: `rsync -a static/fonts/ site/assets/fonts/` in the build script
Sam: ok I'll add both: a `scripts/ensure-assets.sh` that copies fonts and a `site/_headers` entry. I'll push to the branch in a minute
docs-bot: Deploy preview created for branch `sam/docs-fix-fonts` — https://deploy-preview-124--docs.redwood.ai.netlify.app :rocket:
Maria: for reviewers, tag `@docs` and `@eng-runtime` please. We should also ping @eng-oncall if it lands before 9am next day
Jake: can we avoid immediate merge? There are two other docs deploys scheduled today, push to merge window 5pm PT to avoid overlapping preview churn
Priya: Agreed. Also add a short note in the PR description: why headers are needed and that it's limited to `assets/fonts/` so it's audit-friendly
Sam: pushing now. Command I ran locally to validate: `pipx run mkdocs build --clean && python -m http.server --directory site 8000` then open `http://127.0.0.1:8000` to check headers with browser extension
Maria: alternative check: `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8000/assets/fonts/Inter.woff2` should show `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header after build
Jake: CI note: if docs-ci uses a container with different UID, `rsync` might preserve perms weirdly — use `rsync -a --chmod=ugo=rwX` in the script
Priya: sample `_headers` entry I used last time for reference:
```
/assets/fonts/*
  Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
  Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET
```
Sam: pushed branch with two commits, PR is ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
Sam: added reviewers @Maria and @Jake, description explains symlink -> copy and headers limited to fonts
Maria: quick review done, added one nit (shell quoting). Approving after nit fix ✅
Jake: approving too. But hold merge until 17:00 PT as suggested ⏳
docs-bot: docs-ci build started for PR #842
NetlifyBot: Preview updated: https://deploy-preview-124--docs.redwood.ai.netlify.app — Linkcheck passed, but keep an eye on fonts in browser console
Sam: I verified in a fresh incognito window and fonts load now, console is clean — thanks! 🎉
Priya: nice. Add a short note in the migration guide about avoiding symlinks in `static/` and prefer a `make docs-sync-assets` target
Sam: will add that follow-up PR in the morning, and will coordinate merge with release windows
Maria: great teamwork — leaving this thread open until merge occurs
